items.question: Which antibiotic inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis?
items.explanation: Penicillins (beta-lactams) inhibit transpeptidase, blocking peptidoglycan cross-linking in the cell wall.

items.question: Cardiotoxicity is characteristic of which drug?
items.explanation: Doxorubicin (anthracycline) causes dose-dependent cardiomyopathy; dexrazoxane is cardioprotective. Bleomycin causes lung fibrosis.

items.question: Antidote for methanol poisoning is?
items.explanation: Fomepizole (or ethanol) inhibits alcohol dehydrogenase, preventing toxic formic acid formation in methanol poisoning.

items.question: Activated charcoal is most useful when given?
items.explanation: Activated charcoal adsorbs many drugs if given within about 1 hour of ingestion. It does not bind iron, lithium or alcohols.

items.question: Paul Ehrlich developed which early antisyphilitic drug?
items.explanation: Paul Ehrlich introduced Salvarsan (arsphenamine) for syphilis, founding the concept of targeted chemotherapy.

*PharmaCraft Daily - 23 Oct 2026*

🎓 *MBBS* (Chemotherapy)
Q: Which antibiotic inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis?
Ans: Penicillin
Why: Penicillins (beta-lactams) inhibit transpeptidase, blocking peptidoglycan cross-linking in the cell wall.

🩺 *NEET PG* (Anticancer)
Q: Cardiotoxicity is characteristic of which drug?
Ans: Doxorubicin
Why: Doxorubicin (anthracycline) causes dose-dependent cardiomyopathy; dexrazoxane is cardioprotective. Bleomycin causes lung fibrosis.

🏥 *INI-CET* (Toxicology)
Q: Antidote for methanol poisoning is?
Ans: Fomepizole or ethanol
Why: Fomepizole (or ethanol) inhibits alcohol dehydrogenase, preventing toxic formic acid formation in methanol poisoning.

🌍 *FMGE* (Toxicology)
Q: Activated charcoal is most useful when given?
Ans: Within 1 hour of ingestion
Why: Activated charcoal adsorbs many drugs if given within about 1 hour of ingestion. It does not bind iron, lithium or alcohols.

🔬 *MD Pharmacology* (History of Pharmacology)
Q: Paul Ehrlich developed which early antisyphilitic drug?
Ans: Salvarsan
Why: Paul Ehrlich introduced Salvarsan (arsphenamine) for syphilis, founding the concept of targeted chemotherapy.
